nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed graph, let $B$ be one of the blocks returned by the strongly connected components algorithm on $G$, and let $m$ be a vertex of $B$. Then for every vertex $v$ of $G$, the vertices $m$ and $v$ are strongly connected (each is reachable from the other) if and only if $v$ lies in $B$.
nodes.title: Each computed component is a full mutual-reachability class

nodes.summary: In a directed graph $G$, a list $S$ of vertices reaches a list $T$ of vertices when some vertex of $S$ reaches some vertex of $T$ by a directed path in $G$, possibly of length zero.
nodes.title: Reachability between components

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed graph and let $S$ and $T$ be blocks returned by the strongly connected components algorithm on $G$. If some vertex of $S$ reaches some vertex of $T$ and some vertex of $T$ reaches some vertex of $S$, then $S = T$.
nodes.title: The condensation of the computed components is acyclic

nodes.summary: For every directed graph $G$, the list of blocks returned by the strongly connected components algorithm on $G$ is an SCC partition of $G$: every block is nonempty and contains no vertex twice, blocks at different positions of the list are disjoint, every vertex of $G$ lies in some block, two vertices lie in a common block exactly when they are strongly connected, and for every vertex $m$ of a block $B$ and every…
nodes.title: The computed components form the SCC partition

nodes.summary: For every directed graph $G$, each block returned by the strongly connected components algorithm on $G$ contains no vertex more than once.
nodes.title: Computed components have no repeated vertices

nodes.summary: For every directed graph $G$, each block returned by the strongly connected components algorithm on $G$ contains at least one vertex.
nodes.title: Computed components are nonempty

nodes.summary: For every directed graph $G$, any two blocks at different positions of the list returned by the strongly connected components algorithm on $G$ have no vertex in common.
nodes.title: Computed components are pairwise disjoint

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed graph and let $v_1, \dots, v_n$ be its vertices in decreasing order of finishing time in a depth-first search of the whole graph that takes its roots in the vertex order of $G$. For each $i$, let $C_i$ be the list of those $v_j$, in increasing order of $j$, such that $v_i$ and $v_j$ are strongly connected (tested by two depth-first searches). The output is the list $C_1, \dots, C_n$ with…
nodes.title: Strongly connected components algorithm

nodes.summary: A list $\mathcal{B}$ of vertex lists of a directed graph $G$ has an acyclic condensation when, for all $S, T \in \mathcal{B}$, if some vertex of $S$ reaches some vertex of $T$ in $G$ and some vertex of $T$ reaches some vertex of $S$, then $S = T$. That is, reachability between the blocks is antisymmetric.
nodes.title: Acyclic condensation

nodes.summary: In the whole-graph traversal `dfsAll` of a directed graph $G$, every edge $(x, y)$ of $G$ leads to a descendant of $x$ in the depth-first spanning forest or to a vertex discovered before $x$. In Tarjan's terms, the edges that are not tree arcs run from ancestors to descendants, from descendants to ancestors (fronds), or between subtrees (cross-links), and a cross-link $(v, w)$ always has…
nodes.title: Edges of a depth-first search go to descendants or to earlier vertices

nodes.summary: In the whole-graph traversal `dfsAll` of a directed graph, two strongly connected vertices have a common ancestor in the depth-first spanning forest that lies in their strongly connected component.
nodes.title: Strongly connected vertices have a common ancestor in their component (depth-first search)

nodes.summary: The whole-graph traversal `dfsAll` of a directed graph, numbered by preorder index, has the four numbering properties of depth-first search: its tree arcs are edges, ancestors are numbered first, descendants are numbered consecutively, and every edge leads to a descendant or to an earlier vertex.
nodes.title: The repository's depth-first search has the numbering properties of depth-first search

nodes.summary: In the whole-graph traversal `dfsAll` of a directed graph, numbered by preorder index, a vertex $v$ is the first vertex of its strongly connected component if and only if $\mathrm{LOWLINK}(v) = v$.
nodes.title: Tarjan's lowlink test for the repository's depth-first search

nodes.summary: In the whole-graph traversal `dfsAll adj`, an ancestor's preorder index is at most its descendant's (Tarjan, *Depth-first search and linear graph algorithms*, SIAM J. Comput. 1(2) (1972), §3: "If `u` is an ancestor of `v` in the spanning tree `T` of `P`, then `u < v`", vertices being identified with their numbers).
nodes.title: Ancestors are discovered first in the repository's depth-first search

nodes.summary: In the whole-graph traversal `dfsAll adj`, every recorded `(child, parent)` pair is an edge from parent to child.
nodes.title: Tree arcs of the repository's depth-first search are graph edges

nodes.summary: In the whole-graph traversal `dfsAll`, numbered by preorder index, if $a$ is an ancestor of $d$, every vertex whose number lies between those of $a$ and $d$ is a descendant of $a$. The proof is an invariant of the search machine: once a vertex discovered after $a$ is not a descendant of $a$, all descendants of $a$ have already been discovered.
nodes.title: Descendants are numbered consecutively in depth-first search

nodes.summary: Under the numbering properties, two vertices $v$ and $w$ of the same strongly connected component have a common ancestor in the depth-first spanning forest that belongs to the component: the first vertex of the component.
nodes.title: Common ancestor of strongly connected vertices

nodes.summary: For a directed graph $G$, tree arcs `parents` and a numbering $\mathrm{num}$ of the vertices, `IsDFSNumbering` collects the four properties of a depth-first search that Tarjan's analysis of strong connectivity uses:
nodes.title: Numbering properties of depth-first search

nodes.summary: Under the numbering properties, a vertex $v$ is the [first vertex of its strongly connected component](is-first-in-component.md), that is, the root of the subtree formed by the component, if and only if $\mathrm{LOWLINK}(v) = v$.
nodes.title: Tarjan's lowlink test for component roots

nodes.summary: `IsFirstInComponent` holds for $v$ when $\mathrm{num}(v) \le \mathrm{num}(w)$ for every $w$ strongly connected to $v$: $v$ is the first vertex of its component reached by the search. By Corollary 11 it is the root of the subtree that the component forms in the depth-first spanning forest, which Tarjan calls the root of the component.
nodes.title: First vertex of a strongly connected component

nodes.summary: A list $\mathcal{B}$ of vertex lists is an SCC partition of a directed graph $G$ when every block of $\mathcal{B}$ is nonempty and contains no vertex twice, blocks at different positions of $\mathcal{B}$ are disjoint, a vertex lies in some block exactly when it is a vertex of $G$, two vertices lie in a common block exactly when they are strongly connected (each is reachable from the other), and for every block $B$,…
nodes.title: SCC partition

nodes.summary: Tarjan defines $\mathrm{LOWLINK}(v)$ as the smallest-numbered vertex that is in the same strongly connected component as $v$ and is reachable from $v$ by traversing zero or more tree arcs followed by at most one frond or cross-link. `LowlinkEqSelf` says that this minimum is $v$: for every descendant $d$ of $v$ and every edge $(d, w)$ with $w$ strongly connected to $v$, $\mathrm{num}(v) \le \mathrm{num}(w)$.…
nodes.title: `LOWLINK(v) = v`

nodes.summary: For a directed graph $G$ and a vertex $v$, $v$ belongs to some block of the computed strongly connected components of $G$ if and only if $v$ occurs in the vertex enumeration of $G$.
nodes.title: The computed components cover the vertex list

nodes.summary: For a directed graph $G$ and vertices $u$ and $v$, the executable mutual-reachability test on $u$ and $v$ returns true if and only if $u$ and $v$ are strongly connected in $G$.
nodes.title: The mutual-reachability test is correct

nodes.summary: For a directed graph $G$ and vertices $u$ and $v$, the test returns true exactly when $v$ occurs in the preorder of the depth-first search of $G$ from the single root $u$, and $u$ occurs in the preorder of the depth-first search of $G$ from the single root $v$.
nodes.title: Executable mutual-reachability test

nodes.summary: For a directed graph $G$ and vertices $u$ and $v$, some block of the computed strongly connected components of $G$ contains both $u$ and $v$ if and only if $u$ and $v$ are strongly connected in $G$.
nodes.title: Vertices share a computed component exactly when strongly connected

nodes.summary: Under the numbering properties, let $v$ and $w$ be strongly connected and let $u$ be a common ancestor of $v$ and $w$ in the depth-first spanning forest whose number is at least that of every common ancestor. Then $u$ lies in the strongly connected component of $v$ and $w$.
nodes.title: The highest-numbered common ancestor lies in the component

nodes.summary: Under the numbering properties (only the first is used), if $a$ is an ancestor of $b$, $b$ an ancestor of $d$, and $a$ and $d$ are strongly connected, then $b$ and $d$ are strongly connected: $b$ reaches $d$ along tree arcs, and $d$ reaches $a$, which reaches $b$ along tree arcs. So the vertices of a strongly connected component form a subtree of the depth-first spanning forest.
nodes.title: Strongly connected components are closed under tree paths

nodes.summary: In a directed graph $G$, every vertex is strongly connected to itself.
nodes.title: Strong connectivity is reflexive

nodes.summary: For a directed graph $G$, the relation on the vertices of $G$ that holds between $u$ and $v$ exactly when $u$ and $v$ are strongly connected in $G$, packaged as an equivalence relation.
nodes.title: Strong connectivity as an equivalence relation

nodes.summary: In a directed adjacency graph $G$, vertices $u$ and $v$ are strongly connected when $v$ is reachable from $u$ and $u$ is reachable from $v$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Strongly connected vertices

nodes.summary: In a directed graph $G$, if $u$ is strongly connected to $v$, then $v$ is strongly connected to $u$.
nodes.title: Strong connectivity is symmetric

nodes.summary: In a directed graph $G$, if $u$ is strongly connected to $v$ and $v$ is strongly connected to $w$, then $u$ is strongly connected to $w$.
nodes.title: Strong connectivity is transitive

nodes.summary: Under the numbering properties, if $u$ is the [first vertex of its strongly connected component](is-first-in-component.md), then every vertex of the component is a descendant of $u$. Follow a path from $u$ to a vertex $x$ of the component: all its vertices lie in the component, and an edge from a descendant of $u$ either leads to a descendant or to a vertex numbered before its tail, hence, by minimality of $u$ and…
nodes.title: The first vertex of a component is an ancestor of all of it

nodes.summary: For a list `parents` of tree arcs, recorded as (child, parent) pairs, `TreeAncestor parents a d` holds when $d$ is reached from $a$ by zero or more tree arcs: $a$ is an ancestor of $d$, every vertex being an ancestor of itself. This is Tarjan's relation $a \overset{*}{\to} d$ in the spanning tree of a depth-first search.
nodes.title: Ancestor in a depth-first spanning forest

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
